subject.title: feat(backup): add exclude patterns, --smart-exclude, and protected path guards [ai]

question: Should backup create ever auto-load `.backupignore` without an explicit exclude flag, or must exclude behavior remain opt-in for existing users?
rationale: This is a user-facing backup compatibility and security choice: the safer default is source-backed, but accepting auto-load semantics would be an intentional product decision rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Keep excludes explicit
options.body: Require a flag or other explicit user action before `.backupignore` can affect backup contents, preserving existing no-flag backup behavior.

options.title: Accept auto-load semantics
options.body: Allow `.backupignore` to affect ordinary backups, but require maintainer-approved docs, upgrade proof, and recovery guidance.

options.title: Restart from a fresh PR
options.body: Close this conflicting branch and ask for a smaller rebased replacement that resolves the product choice up front.

recommendation.title: Keep excludes explicit
recommendation.body: Require a flag or other explicit user action before `.backupignore` can affect backup contents, preserving existing no-flag backup behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest visible recent contribution count across the central backup command/test files and is a good owner for the compatibility decision.
